summary: Otto Höfler worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Vienna (PhD 1920–1926 under Rudolf Much; Habilitation ~1928–1931), Lund, and Kiel. He held posts at Uppsala, Lund, Kiel, Munich, and Vienna (1957–1971).

Otto Jahn specialized in history and archaeology. He studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Berlin. He later held positions at Greifswald (~1839–1842), Kiel (~1842–1847), Leipzig (~1847–1851), and Bonn (~1855–1869), succeeding Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker in 1854.

Otto Maenchen-Helfen was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna, Gothenburg, and Leipzig under August Conrady. His career included posts at the Marx-Engels-Lenin Institute, Mills College, and UC Berkeley (1947–1962).

Otto Neugebauer worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Graz, Munich, Copenhagen, and Göttingen (PhD ~1922–1926), and under Boris Turayev. He held professorships at Göttingen, Copenhagen, Brown University (1939–1969), and the Institute for Advanced Study.

Otto Rosenberg specialized in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and sinology. He studied at Saint Petersburg under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Sergey Oldenburg, at Bonn under Hermann Jacobi, and with Rudolf Lange. He served as professor at Saint Petersburg State University from 1911 to 1919.

Otto Stein was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at Charles University under Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda. He held posts at the Oriental Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences and at Charles University as professor of Indian philology (1930–1939).

Otto Strauß was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Munich, Berlin, and Kiel under Paul Deussen and Hermann Oldenberg. He held professorships at Kiel (1920), the University of Calcutta (1913–1920), and the University of Breslau (1928–1935).

Otto von Böhtlingk was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg, Berlin under Franz Bopp, and Bonn under Christian Lassen. He held long-term posts at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences (1842–1868) and the University of Jena (~1868–1885).

Owen Flanagan is a philosopher working in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed studies at Fordham University and Boston University before joining Duke University, where he served as Professor of Philosophy beginning around 1996.
Ozer Taye was a scholar who studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

P. A. Payutto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his bachelor's degree in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1958–1962), later serving there as Associate Dean (~1964–1973), and was Tipitaka Acharaya at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1995.

P. D. Premasiri works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ceylon, Cambridge, and Hawaiʻi (PhD under Eliot Deutsch). He held multiple posts at the University of Ceylon, including department head (1997–2004) and professor (attested 2010).

P. K. Mukhopadhyay is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served as a Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and was a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 2009).

P. Pratap Kumar is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served as a Professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal (attested 2010) and as a Visiting Professor at Colorado College (attested 2010).
P. S. Chandrasekharan is an Indologist who worked as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the supervision of V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).
P. S. Sivaswami Iyer was an Indologist who studied at Presidency College, Chennai (~1880–1884). In 1927, he served as the President of the Editorial Board for the Journal of Oriental Research.

P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bishop Heber College, IASE, and the University of Madras. He served as Principal of Rajah's College, Thiruvaiyaru, and Head of Sanskrit at Annamalai University (1942–1947).
P. T. Narasimhachar worked in Indology. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1923–1926), where he was a student of Mysore Hiriyanna.

Padma Subrahmanyam is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Ethiraj College for Women, Stella Maris College, and completed research under Tiruvengadu Narayanayajwa Ramachandran at Annamalai University (~1972–1979).
Padmanabh S. Jaini was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 1977–2002; Professor Emeritus attested 2016).
